title: PowerPoint on desktop: reference a Teams meeting or chat when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: Hold: licensing is not the only documented way to control Copilot in desktop PowerPoint; connected-experience privacy controls can also disable it. Microsoft also documents the user-permission boundary and the limitation that Copilot does not recognize sensitivity labels protecting Teams meetings and chats, which the briefing incorrectly leaves unresolved.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: The release-notes entry covers roadmap ids 555885, 555884 and 555883.
No Microsoft Learn page dedicated to this specific feature was found.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode reference Teams meeting chat; Copilot PowerPoint Teams meeting chat references license prerequisite billing meter. Results describe this feature in release notes, not a dedicated Learn article.

claims.claim: Microsoft presents the feature as avoiding manual summarising or transferring notes.
claims.quote: This makes it easier to turn Teams conversations, meeting outcomes, and chat discussions into presentation-ready content without manually summarizing or transferring notes.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The feature's default state is unknown.
claims.quote: You can now reference a Teams meeting or chat when creating a presentation with Agent Mode in PowerPoint. Enter a prompt that references the Teams meeting or chat you want to use in your presentation.
claims.fix: Set defaultState to 'user-opt-in': the launched capability is available and is used when the user chooses to reference a meeting or chat in a prompt; the targeted control searches found no dedicated admin switch. Replace 'Microsoft has not stated what happens on arrival' with 'Users choose whether to reference a Teams meeting or chat when creating a presentation.'

claims.claim: No source says this feature replaces or changes existing workflows without a user choosing it.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint reference Teams meeting chat default automatically rollout admin enabled. Opened roadmap record and release-notes feature entry; both describe a capability users can choose, not a replacement workflow.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Security & identity
claims.claim: The release-notes entry itself does not specify whose permissions determine access to the referenced content.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Teams permissions Copilot. Read the release-notes entry: it describes referencing securely, without identifying the access-check identity. Product privacy documentation separately supplies the user boundary.

claims.claim: The release-notes entry itself gives no details about sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint generated presentation sensitivity label inherit meetings chats. Read release-notes entry: no label details. Architecture and Purview documentation separately explain the Teams-label limitation.

claims.claim: Anyone who later receives the presentation file can see whatever was drawn from the meeting or chat.
claims.quote:
encryption can also restrict what actions specified people can take on the content.
Protect content in Office apps across different platforms and devices. Supported by Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook
claims.fix: Replace the universal recipient claim with 'Sharing the generated presentation can expose reused Teams content to its permitted readers.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sensitivity-labels for the protection of PowerPoint content.

claims.claim: The Teams source and the generated deck are governed separately rather than automatically sharing the meeting or chat label.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels that protect Teams meetings and chat aren't currently recognized by Copilot and agents. For example, data returned from a meeting chat or channel chat won't display an associated sensitivity label
claims.fix: Replace 'The Teams source and the deck are governed separately' with 'Sensitivity labels protecting Teams meetings and chats are not currently recognized by Copilot and agents, and cannot be inherited by destination content; this limitation does not apply to labeled meeting invites, responses and calendar events.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ai-m365-copilot-considerations.

claims.claim: The release-notes feature entry describes no action outside creating the presentation.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode reference Teams meeting chat. Read the complete release-notes entry: its Try this procedure ends with Copilot creating a presentation; it describes no external action.

claims.where: licensing.notes; controls[0].governs; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence gives access to the full Copilot experience in PowerPoint and the other named Office apps.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents an in-app Copilot experience without the add-on licence, with fair use limits on some features.
claims.quote: You don't have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license but can use Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote. Some features are subject to fair use limits.

claims.claim: Chat experiences in Word, Excel and PowerPoint vary by user licence and tenant configuration.
claims.quote: Chat experiences in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint vary depending on the user's license and tenant configuration.

claims.claim: This feature has a mixed licensing model.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint Teams meeting chat references license prerequisite billing meter; PowerPoint Agent Mode referencing Teams meeting chat license required. Read overview, requirements and service description; none assigns this feature a mixed entitlement.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to 'included' for this new option inside Copilot in PowerPoint, and retain the product-level qualification: 'The Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on licence provides the full Copilot experience in PowerPoint. Microsoft also documents an in-app experience without that add-on; the release-notes entry does not specify which experience includes Teams meeting or chat references.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/copilot-overview.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The exact licence entitlement for this specific Teams-reference feature is not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: PowerPoint Agent Mode referencing Teams meeting chat license required Microsoft 365 Copilot Premium. Read release notes, overview, requirements and service description; no specific entitlement for this reference option. Copilot-app agents are a different surface.

claims.claim: No meter or separate price specific to this feature is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint Teams meeting chat references license prerequisite billing meter. Read release notes, overview, requirements, pay-as-you-go meters excerpt and Copilot Credits services excerpt; none names a meter for this in-app reference option.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Low rates the indirect administrative cost because no additional cost specific to this change is published.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint Teams meeting chat references license prerequisite billing meter. Read product licensing and meter material; no new charge for this option is stated. SCHEMA permits low for known admin-time cost while feature-specific licensing is unpublished.

claims.claim: The release-notes feature entry names no prerequisites beyond starting Copilot and referencing content in a prompt.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint Teams meeting chat references license prerequisite. Read full release-notes entry; its procedure names PowerPoint, Copilot and a prompt, with no separate prerequisite section.

claims.claim: Rollout mechanics are not stated beyond the Launched status.
claims.quote: Copilot features are introduced using a safe deployment model, gradually rolling out to a subset of users within a tenant before expanding across the organization.
claims.fix: Replace 'Rollout mechanics are not stated beyond the Launched status' with 'The roadmap status is Launched. The release notes describe Copilot features generally as gradually rolling out to a subset of users within a tenant before expanding across the organisation.'

claims.claim: Licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Users > Active users > user > Licenses and Apps > Licenses.
claims.quote: go to the Users > Active users page. Select the row of the user that you want to assign a license to. In the right pane, select Licenses and Apps. Expand the Licenses section, select the boxes for the licenses that you want to assign

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a licence using Microsoft Graph PowerShell.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: Assigning licences requires at least License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: You must be at least a License or User Administrator to assign licenses.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no dedicated tenant UI or API switch that disables only Teams meeting or chat references in PowerPoint Agent Mode.
claims.quote: Searched: Manage disable Copilot in PowerPoint Agent Mode Teams references admin switch; Microsoft Graph PowerShell policy disable Teams meeting chat reference PowerPoint Copilot. Read release notes, overview and privacy controls; no dedicated reference-only switch.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The user's Copilot licence is the only documented lever for controlling this desktop capability.
claims.quote:
If you turn off connected experiences that analyze your content on devices in your organization, Microsoft Copilot features won't be available to your users in the following apps:
Excel
OneNote
Outlook
PowerPoint
Word
claims.fix: Remove both 'the only lever today' and 'the only documented lever' conclusions. Replace them with 'The licence row governs access to the full Copilot experience, not this feature alone. Connected-experience privacy controls can also disable Copilot in desktop PowerPoint more broadly.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-privacy.

claims.claim: Removing the add-on licence affects access to the full Copilot experience rather than only this reference feature.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.where: rationale: risk; Open questions: user access
claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented a permission rule governing this Copilot reference capability.
claims.quote: Permissions come first. Copilot only summarizes or references content that the user is already authorized to access.
claims.fix: Remove the permission-rule absence from the risk rationale and the question asking whether Copilot can reference inaccessible content. State 'Copilot only summarizes or references content the user is already authorised to access.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/architecture-data-protection-auditing. Pilot advice can remain as validation, not as an undocumented product boundary.

claims.where: rationale: risk; Open questions: sensitivity labels; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: How Copilot handles sensitivity labels protecting referenced Teams meetings and chats is undocumented.
claims.quote: copying chat data can't be prevented for a destination item, and the sensitivity label can't be inherited. This limitation doesn't apply to meeting invites, responses, and calendar events that are protected by sensitivity labels.
claims.fix: Remove the label-handling absence from the rationale and resolve the label-inheritance part of the open question with 'Copilot and agents do not currently recognize sensitivity labels protecting Teams meetings and chats, and those labels cannot be inherited by destination content. This limitation does not apply to labeled meeting invites, responses and calendar events.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/ai-m365-copilot-considerations. Narrow the pilot instruction to checking the generated deck's protection rather than discovering an undocumented inheritance rule.
